titulo: Accusative and prepositions of place: Wo? × Wohin?: In, an, auf: where and where to

aula.titulo: Accusative and prepositions of place: Wo? × Wohin?
aula.objetivo: Use the prepositions that take the accusative (durch, für, gegen, ohne, um) and the nine two-way prepositions, choosing the dative (Wo?, no movement) or the accusative (Wohin?, movement toward a destination).

sessao.titulo: In, an, auf: where and where to

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: compare the pairs in the table: «Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch» / «Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch»; «Die Lampe steht neben dem Bett» / «Ich stelle die Lampe neben das Bett». STEP 2: which sentence describes where something IS, and which describes moving it somewhere? STEP 3: which case appears in each? STEP 4: now look at these: «Ich fahre mit dem Bus», «Ich komme aus der Schule», «Ich gehe zum Arzt», «Das Geschenk ist für dich», «Ich gehe ohne ihn». Which case comes after mit, aus and zu? And after für and ohne? STEP 5: «zum» is the merger of which two words? Check your answers in the next blocks.

tabela.wohin: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.

tabela.wo: Die Lampe steht neben dem Bett.
tabela.wohin: Ich stelle die Lampe neben das Bett.

blocos.titulo: The nine two-way prepositions: the golden rule
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: nine prepositions change case depending on the question: an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen. STEP 2: GOLDEN RULE: if the question is WO? (where — NO movement toward a goal), use the DATIVE; if it's WOHIN? (where to — MOVEMENT toward a goal), use the ACCUSATIVE. STEP 3: in this session, the three most common: «in» (in, into), «an» (at, on — touching a vertical surface), «auf» (on, onto — on top of a horizontal surface). STEP 4: contractions: in dem = im; an dem = am; in das = ins; an das = ans; auf das = aufs. STEP 5: the article shows the difference: masculine Wo? «dem», Wohin? «den»; feminine Wo? «der», Wohin? «die»; neuter Wo? «dem», Wohin? «das». STEP 6: careful: «Ich bin im Garten» (I'm in the garden — location) × «Ich gehe in den Garten» (I'm going into the garden — movement).
blocos.comparacao: English often marks the difference with two words: "in" vs "into", "on" vs "onto". German uses the SAME preposition («in», «auf») and lets the case show whether there's movement: «im Garten» = in the garden, «in den Garten» = into the garden.
